reasons.A: Closest movement: runs of short declaratives reporting his views in free indirect speech, a dry and understated narrator who admits the point to him, plain diction with sparing semicolons, as in the passage.
reasons.C: Short reported sentences and a wry closing quip catch the irony, but the added similes and staged gestures (sea captain, coachman, the cup) and the epigram 'A thief took; a forger earned' push towards a performed wit the passage doesn't have.
reasons.B: Longer, more elaborate periodic sentences, an exclamation and a dramatised outburst, and a moralising close ('Remove the victims...') give it an editorialising stance that the passage's lighter, deadpan irony does not show.
